ctx: Galatians is Paul's most urgent letter. He skips his usual thanksgiving and goes straight to the charge:

ctx.q: I marvel that so quickly you are deserting from the One having called you in the grace of Christ to another gospel

ctx: . Churches he had planted were being turned toward a different message by teachers who came after him.
Chapters 1 and 2 are Paul's defense, and they are built on the law of witness. He tells how he laid his message before the leaders in Jerusalem,

ctx.q: lest somehow I might be running or had run in vain

ctx: , and how James, Cephas and John gave him
. His gospel was confirmed by other voices, as the rule requires.

inv.q: even if we or an angel out of heaven should preach a gospel to you contrary to what we preached to you, let him be accursed

inv: . Paul names three possible sources of a false gospel: another teacher, himself, and a messenger from heaven. The highest authority conceivable goes into the test. If Paul himself changed the message, the Galatians were to reject him.
The measure is not the speaker. It is

inv.q: faith having been delivered once for all to the saints

inv: seen from the receiving end: a message that was delivered, a people who received it, and a standard that does not move when a new voice arrives. Rank cannot be a witness. An apostle, an angel, a scholar, a council, a bestselling author: each is one voice, and one voice is not enough.

Put the week together. Deuteronomy gave the rule: two or three witnesses. Jesus submitted to it. The Bereans applied it to an apostle. Jude called a witness from a book the Ethiopian canon kept. Jesus listed five witnesses and counted Moses among them. Revelation shows what the world does to faithful witnesses. And Paul turns the rule on himself. Scripture is not a stack of statements to be believed on authority. It is a body of testimony that confirms itself, and it asks the reader to take part in the checking.
One warning from the Ethiopian canon names what the test protects against:

inv.q: sinners will alter and pervert the words of righteousness in many ways

inv: . Alteration is the threat. That is why the words of the testimony matter, and why this archive keeps them open to read.
